# API fixtures

## Signal fixtures

These are **captured from production**, not hand-authored and not generated by
populating the Go structs with chosen values.

`signals-overview.json` is the verbatim body of
`GET /api/v1/signals/overview` from the deployed stack, captured 2026-09-10
against commit `4fd27ba`.

## Why this file is captured rather than written

Three consecutive rounds of adversarial review found the same defect in this
directory: a fixture describing a payload the server cannot emit, with every
test passing green against it.

* Round 1 invented the `/markets/numeraires` shape entirely (`code`/`series_code`
  /`note` where Go emits `key`/`series`/`notes[]`). 51 tests passed against a
  page that could not load at all.
* Round 2 invented six per-market cost hurdles (2.4%, 0.35%, 0.5%, 1.0%) that
  `app/core/costs.py` refuses to produce — in production every non-gold asset
  resolves to the same 2.2% assumption.
* Round 3 invented `omitted_factors: []` for `IR_GOLD_18K`, which
  `app/signals/universe.py` cannot return: gold always omits `gold_fund_flow`.

Each round the fixture was regenerated by hand and each round it drifted again,
because a human choosing plausible values is exactly the step that introduces
the invention. Capturing removes that step.

A fixture that invents server behaviour is worse than no fixture: it does not
merely fail to catch the bug, it manufactures confidence that the bug is absent.

## Refreshing

Capture the live payload rather than editing this file:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  http://<host>:8088/api/v1/signals/overview \
  | python3 -m json.tool > frontend/src/test/fixtures/signals-overview.json
```

If a test then fails, the contract changed — read the diff before touching the
test, because the fixture is now the more trustworthy of the two.


## Screener fixtures (`stocks-screen-*.json`)

`GET /api/v1/stocks/screen` had not been deployed when these were needed, so
they could not be captured with `curl`. They were **emitted by the Go code that
serves the endpoint**, not written by hand:

* The roster metadata in every row — symbol, `name_fa`, sector, board, ISIN,
  `bar_count`, `first_bar`/`last_bar`, the whole `adjustment` block and each
  instrument's `notes` — is **verbatim from a payload captured from production
  `GET /api/v1/stocks`** on 2026-09-10 at commit `7728ad1` (20 instruments,
  کچاد seeded disabled).
* That roster was fed to `equities.buildScreenResponse` — the same pure
  function `Handler.Screen` calls — together with the real
  `relvalue.Converter`, and the result was serialised with `encoding/json`. So
  every field name, every null, every `*_reason` sentence, the `absent_metrics`
  prose, the `excluded` block, `price_basis` and `warnings` are the server's
  own output rather than a human's idea of it.
* The generator was injected into `package equities` with `go test -overlay`,
  so nothing was added to `backend-go/`. Only two things in it are invented:
  the stored **bars** (a deterministic walk on `final_close`, with one
  corporate-action factor step per instrument and halted sessions carried at
  the reference price) and the **numéraire quotes** (daily toman quotes for
  `USD_IRT` and `IR_GOLD_18K`). Both are INPUTS. No output field is authored.

The three files differ only in what was asked of that code:

| file | request | what it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stocks-screen-1y-irr.json` | `period=1y&numeraire=IRR` | the default view; ذوب is halted for all but one session of the window, so its return, volatility and drawdown are null **with reasons** |
| `stocks-screen-3m-usd.json` | `period=3m&numeraire=USD&sort=return&order=desc` | `numeraire_series`, the per-row `conversion` block, metrics measured in USD |
| `stocks-screen-1y-nogold.json` | `period=1y&numeraire=IRR` against a deployment with **no gold series ingested** | `price_gold_grams: null` carrying the numéraire engine's own reason on every row |

### Refreshing

Once the endpoint is deployed, prefer a capture, exactly as above:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  'http://<host>:8088/api/v1/stocks/screen?period=1y&numeraire=IRR' \
  | python3 -m json.tool > frontend/src/test/fixtures/stocks-screen-1y-irr.json
```

If a test then fails, the contract changed — read the diff before touching the
test.
